top_stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Steps Down Amid Scandal
points: Jensen Huang resigned/is being replaced after acknowledging extramarital affairs, including with an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom U.S. intelligence suspects of Chinese espionage.
Finance chief Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while Nvidia's board works with an outside search firm to find a permanent replacement; chairman Harvey Jones leads the board.
Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% and the company has lost over $1 trillion in market value this month, marking the most serious leadership crisis in its history.
China dismissed espionage allegations against the executive as 'smears.'

unique_angles.point: Huang's exit would reduce scrutiny from lawmakers, investors, customers, and staff over personal conduct, with ripple effects across the semiconductor and AI industries.
Huang had led the company for 33 years since co-founding it; incident raises broader questions about corporate espionage and executive vetting in semiconductor firms.

top_stories.title: Google Launches Gemini Decision 1 / Decisions API
points: New specialized model answers yes/no, multiple-choice, and rubric-scoring questions (closed-set classification: picking from a fixed list of possible answers) instead of generating free-form text.
Processes up to 1,000 such decisions in a single pass, across text, images, audio, video, and PDF inputs, responding in 150–250ms on average.
Priced at $0.10 per million (TLDR cites per 2 million) input tokens with no charge for output tokens—roughly five times cheaper than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite.
Accepts up to 256,000 tokens (roughly 190,000 words) of context; available via the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.
Outperformed competing decision-focused models (OpenAI's Decisions API and TypeSafe's Jev) on most benchmarks tested.

unique_angles.point: Framed as part of a broader 'B2A economy' (business-to-agent) trend in AI tooling.
Because it skips generating extra tokens, applications can act directly on probability scores, useful for high-throughput production systems.
Signals an industry shift away from expensive general-purpose chatbots toward lightweight, task-specific models for narrow enterprise use cases.

top_stories.title: AWS Releases Public Emulator for Local AI-Agent Testing
points: AWS Emulator lets AI coding agents build and test software against 200+ local AWS service stand-ins without hitting real cloud infrastructure, avoiding cost and delay.
Code is publicly available; autonomous agents reportedly wrote the entire emulator themselves.
Shifts engineers' role toward deciding what to build and validating correctness rather than writing routine code.
Does not yet simulate throttling, outages, or regional differences found in real AWS environments.

unique_angles.point: Highlighted as part of a broader shift where engineering leaders must personally re-engage with coding to stay relevant as agents accelerate implementation.

items.title: OpenAI's Proof Verification Process
points: An OpenAI-appointed expert committee confirmed a proof of quantum Yang-Mills theory (a foundational mathematical framework underlying the Standard Model of particle physics), validating one of its cornerstone results.
The committee was formed after backlash over OpenAI releasing 700+ AI-generated mathematical proofs in a single day in October.
Committee members admit the proof is too long and complex for immediate full human comprehension, raising concerns about how such verification can scale.
Some mathematicians argue the oversight process is unnecessary gatekeeping rather than genuine rigorous validation.

items.title: Blue Phone and Agent-First Computing
points: Y Combinator-backed startup launched a public beta of 'Blue Phone' at $1,299, running a custom Android OS (Blue OS) on Pixel 10 Pro/XL hardware.
Lets AI agents autonomously handle multi-app workflows and navigate apps directly instead of requiring manual UI taps.
Developers are encouraged to design agent-friendly, API-first or headless interfaces as agents increasingly interact with apps instead of humans.

items.title: GitHub Account Hijacking Wave
points: Over 4,800 GitHub accounts were compromised by malware targeting CI/CD (continuous integration/continuous deployment, the automated pipelines that build and deploy code) pipelines and cloud credentials.
Developers are urged to audit recent commits, revoke exposed tokens, enable multi-factor authentication, and check for unauthorized cloud access.
Risk is amplified as AI agents increasingly write and push code autonomously, meaning a single compromised account can spread damage across infrastructure.

items.title: Engineering Leadership Must Return to Hands-On Coding
points: Will Larson, former CTO of Carta and Calm, says he merged more pull requests (proposed code changes submitted for review) on a 25-person team than in his entire prior career, crediting AI tooling.
He warns traditional middle-management engineering roles may not exist in three years.
Recommended tactics: take on real tickets, ship to production, prioritize technical solutions over hiring, and avoid management structures that isolate leaders from actual implementation.

items.title: Starlink Speed Cap Undermines Ukraine's Drone Defense
points: Starshield (the military version of Starlink) re-imposed a 161 km/h speed limit on satellite connections, crippling Ukraine's systems for intercepting fast-moving drones.
The cap prevents Ukrainian interceptors from reaching Russian Geran-4 drones flying at 300–400 km/h, allowing some strikes to get through.
Ukraine's Defense Ministry had recorded stable links above 400 km/h just three weeks earlier.
Musk says the U.S. government controls Starshield policy, while Washington says only Musk could authorize the restriction—leaving the source of the cap unclear.

items.title: United Airlines Blocks Unauthorized AI Booking Agents
points: United revised its Contract of Carriage to ban unauthorized third-party AI agents from booking, purchasing, or managing travel, including tools embedded in social media, browsers, or travel agencies.
Violations can result in canceled bookings, voided tickets, erased frequent-flyer miles, revoked elite status, and legal action.
AI tools may still be used for research and trip planning as long as they never access United's website, systems, or user credentials.
Bookings made before November 11, 2026 are grandfathered in and won't be canceled.

items.title: Google's AlphaGenome 2 Links DNA Variants to Disease in Specific Cells
points: AlphaGenome 2 predicts how genetic variants affect specific human cell types by analyzing DNA sequences against chosen cell states, including gene activity and methylation (a chemical modification that affects gene activity) patterns.
Trained on over 107 million individual cell profiles from 68 tissues in humans and mice.
Found about 30% of causal disease variants on immune-cell benchmarks, up from 16% in the prior version.
Reproduced an inflammatory bowel disease mechanism by pinpointing the variant overactivating the ETS2 gene in gut cells, aiding precision medicine.

items.title: Tesla Extends Cybertruck Production
points: Tesla extends Cybertruck production through summer 2027 to clear its backlog.
Only the Cyberbeast variant, priced at $110,000, will remain in production.
Manufacturing resources are shifting toward development of the Cybercab.

sections.title: 1. Nvidia Leadership Crisis and Stock Collapse

sections.title: 2. Starlink Speed Cap Undermines Ukraine's Drone Defense
points: Starshield (military Starlink) re-imposed a 161 km/h speed limit on satellite connections, crippling Ukraine's drone interception systems designed to stop Russian Geran-4 drones flying at 300-400 km/h.

The limit prevents high-speed interceptors from reaching targets, allowing some Russian strikes to get through; Ukraine's Defense Ministry had recorded stable links above 400 km/h just three weeks prior.
Musk claims the U.S. government controls Starshield policy, while Washington states only Musk could authorize such restrictions, leaving unclear who imposed the speed cap and why.
The cap directly impacts Ukraine's ability to defend against aerial attacks and represents a significant tactical vulnerability in ongoing warfare.

sections.title: 3. Google's Decision 1 Model Targets Specific AI Use Cases
points: Gemini Decision 1 costs $0.10 per million input tokens with no output charges—approximately five times cheaper than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite—designed for organizations making repetitive yes/no, multiple-choice, or rating decisions.

Unlike general-purpose chatbots, Decision 1 only handles binary and categorical questions, returning terse answers with confidence scores, and accepts up to 256,000 tokens (roughly 190,000 words) of text, audio, images, or video.
The model outperformed TypeSafe's Jev and OpenAI's Decisions API on seven of nine benchmarks, signaling a shift toward specialized, cost-efficient models for narrow business applications.
This move reflects the broader industry trend away from expensive general models toward lightweight, task-specific AI for enterprise efficiency.

sections.title: 4. Google AI Traces Disease DNA to Specific Cell Types
points: AlphaGenome 2 predicts how genetic variants affect specific human cell types by analyzing DNA sequences against chosen cell states, calculating gene activity and methylation patterns unique to each cell.

Trained on over 107 million individual cell profiles from 68 tissues in humans and mice, the model found approximately 30% of causal disease variants on immune-cell benchmarks, up from 16% in the prior version.
The system reproduced an inflammatory bowel disease mechanism by isolating the exact genetic variant overactivating the ETS2 gene in gut cells, enabling precision medicine approaches.
This breakthrough enables researchers to link genetic variants directly to disease in specific tissues, accelerating drug discovery and personalized treatment development.

sections.title: 5. United Airlines Blocks Third-Party AI Booking Agents
points: United revised its Contract of Carriage to forbid unauthorized third-party AI agents from booking, purchasing, or managing travel, covering tools embedded in social media, browsers, and travel agencies.

Violations allow United to cancel bookings, void tickets, erase frequent-flyer miles, revoke elite status, and pursue legal action, citing privacy breaches, account security risks, and potential conflicts with federal aviation rules.

AI research and general trip planning remain permitted if tools never access United's website, systems, or user credentials; all bookings made before November 11, 2026 are grandfathered in and won't be canceled.
The restriction reflects growing airline concerns about uncontrolled automation creating liability and fraud risks while AI agents proliferate in travel booking.
